summary: The NNPC/Seplat JV National Undergraduate Scholarship pays a yearly grant (reported as N200,000 in 2026), renewed if your grades stay good, to students in 200 level or above at federal or state universities in Nigeria. It is limited to a fixed list of courses. Winners are strong students (CGPA 3.5+) who are shortlisted from a short online form and then do well in the scholarship examination.
lookfor: Five O-level credits in one sitting, including English and Mathematics
Studying one of the listed courses at a federal or state university
Performance in the scholarship examination for shortlisted applicants
Accurate, complete details - false or incomplete details lead to disqualification
cycle: Recent calls: Sept 2024 (two-week window), March 2025, and 23 Feb - 13 Mar 2026. The 2026 round has closed; expect the next call around Feb-Apr 2027 with a window of only two to three weeks, so prepare now.

eligibility.q: Are you in 200 level (second year) or above at a federal or state university in Nigeria?
eligibility.no: Private university students are not covered. 100-level students should prepare and apply next year.
Raise your CGPA and apply next year, or look at awards with lower cut-offs (e.g. MTN for blind students has 2.5).

eligibility.q: Do you have at least five O-level credits in ONE sitting, including English and Mathematics?
eligibility.no: Two sittings are not accepted. Consider other awards that accept combined results.

eligibility.q: Is your course on the Seplat list (Accountancy, Agriculture, Architecture, Business Administration, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical/Electronic, Mechanical, Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineering, Computer Science, Economics, Environmental Studies, Geology, Geophysics, Law, Mass Communication, Medicine (and Dentistry in 2026), Ophthalmology/Optometry)?
eligibility.no: Courses outside the list are not eligible. Try MTN (STEM/medicine), Jim Ovia (any course) or SNEPCo (no course list in 2025).

eligibility.q: Are you free of any other scholarship?
eligibility.no: The 2026 call said applicants must not be beneficiaries of another scholarship. Decide which award you will keep.

steps.title: Confirm you meet every rule
steps.why: The list of courses and the one-sitting O-level rule rule out many applicants. Checking now saves wasted effort.
do: Open the 2025 Seplat Energy call and read the eligibility and course list.
Check your O-level certificate: five credits in one sitting including English and Maths?
Check your latest CGPA on your student portal.
Confirm your university is federal or state, not private.
tips: The course list has been stable in 2024, 2025 and 2026; still read the current call in case it changes.
avoid: Applying with a course not on the list - the form may accept it but you will not be shortlisted.
check: I meet all five eligibility rules.

steps.title: Learn the official channels and avoid scams
steps.why: The application link changes almost every year (a bit.ly link in 2024, register.seplatscholarship.com in 2025, the Seplat Growth Academy page in 2026). Fraudsters copy these.
do: Bookmark the News & insights section of seplatenergy.com. The official call is posted there.
Bookmark seplatgrowthacademy.com/scholarship, used for the 2026 round.
When you see a call elsewhere, go to seplatenergy.com yourself and confirm it is posted there before you apply.
Remember: Seplat says the application is FREE.
tips: The application is free. Anyone asking you to pay for a form, 'processing', a test slot or 'guaranteed selection' is a scammer.
Never use an 'agent' or cybercafe operator to apply for you with their email. Use your own email and phone so the funder's messages reach you.
Use your university's scholarship or Students Affairs office to double-check a call.
avoid: Filling a 'Seplat' form on a site that is not linked from seplatenergy.com.
check: I know where the real call is posted.

steps.title: Set a calendar for February to April
steps.why: The window is short (two to three weeks). Students who check weekly from January catch it in time.
do: Add a weekly reminder from 15 January 2027 to check seplatenergy.com news.
Once open, note the closing date and set alarms 7 days and 2 days before it.
Block study time for the scholarship exam in the weeks after the deadline.
Put the SNEPCo (June-Aug) and MTN (Apr-May) calls on the same calendar.
tips: Join your faculty's official notice board or class group - many students hear of the call there first, then verify on the official site.
avoid: Relying only on WhatsApp forwards to know when it opens.
check: I have reminders set from January.

steps.title: Set up a proper email address
steps.why: The call requires a valid personal email. Shortlisting messages go there.
do: Use or create a Gmail/Yahoo address with your real name (e.g. firstname.lastname).
Turn on phone notifications for this email.
Make sure your phone number is active and registered in your name (NIN-linked).
tips: Check spam/promotions folders after you apply.
avoid: Using a shared or cybercafe email.
check: I have a personal email I check daily.

steps.title: Keep your academic papers ready even if the form does not ask
steps.why: In 2026 the first stage was a short form with no uploads, but shortlisted candidates must prove what they typed. If you cannot, you lose the award.
do: Get a signed and stamped copy of your results showing your current CGPA from your department.
Find your O-level certificate or print the online result (the one-sitting result).
Keep your JAMB admission letter, school ID card and NIN slip ready.
Scan all of them into one folder.
tips: Type your CGPA on the form exactly as it appears on your result.
avoid: Rounding up your CGPA or level - verification will catch it.
check: I can prove every detail I will enter.

steps.title: Fill the online form carefully
steps.why: False or incomplete details lead to disqualification, and only shortlisted applicants are contacted.
do: Open the call on seplatenergy.com and follow its link to the form (in 2026 it was via seplatgrowthacademy.com/scholarship).
Enter your names exactly as on your school records.
Fill university, course, level, CGPA, O-level details and contacts.
If an application form PDF is offered (it was in 2025), download it and read it to see all questions first.
Review every answer, then submit and screenshot the confirmation.
tips: Fill it on a laptop if possible; long forms are easy to mistype on a phone.
avoid: Submitting twice - this can look like duplicate entries.
Choosing the wrong course from a drop-down list.

steps.title: Prepare for the scholarship examination
steps.why: Shortlisted applicants sit a scholarship exam. Your score decides who wins.
do: Start practice right after you submit - do not wait for the invitation.
Practise numerical reasoning (percentages, ratios, tables), verbal reasoning and general knowledge questions.
Revise basic Maths and English at secondary-school level.
Do timed sets on a computer to get used to a CBT screen.
tips: Keep an error log and redo questions you got wrong.
avoid: Paying for 'past questions' from strangers that claim to be leaked.
check: I can complete timed practice sets confidently.

steps.title: Watch for the shortlist message
steps.why: Only shortlisted applicants are contacted, often with little notice before the exam.
do: Check your email (including spam) and SMS daily.
When contacted, confirm the exam date, venue or online link, and what to bring.
Plan transport to the centre if needed; aim to arrive early.
If you hear nothing for several weeks after the deadline, assume you were not shortlisted and move on to the next award.
tips: Save the official sender's address so you can tell real messages from fake ones.
avoid: Responding to messages that ask for payment to 'secure' your exam slot.
check: I know how I will be contacted.

steps.title: Sit the exam
steps.why: This is the main selection stage.
do: Bring the ID and documents named in the invitation (school ID, printed invitation).
Arrive early, follow the invigilators' instructions.
Answer easy questions first, then return to hard ones.
tips: Eat and sleep well the night before.
check: I have everything ready the night before.

steps.title: Accept the award and keep it
steps.why: The grant is renewed based on satisfactory academic performance, so winning is only the start.
do: Read the award terms and conditions carefully.
Provide bank details only through the official channel in your award letter.
Keep your CGPA up; send results when asked each session.
If not selected, apply again next year if you still meet the rules.
tips: Keep copies of all award letters for future CVs and applications.
avoid: Ignoring renewal requests - you can lose the grant.

faq.a: Reported as N200,000 a year in the 2026 call, renewable with good performance. Check the current call.

faq.q: Do I need to upload documents?
faq.a: Not at the first stage in 2026, but shortlisted candidates should expect to prove everything they entered.

faq.q: Is it only for Niger Delta students?
faq.a: No. It is a national award for federal and state universities across Nigeria.

faq.q: My course is not on the list. Can I still apply?
faq.a: No. Choose an award with no course restriction, such as Jim Ovia.
No. Seplat states the application is free.

faq.q: When will the next call open?
faq.a: Recent calls opened in September 2024, March 2025 and February 2026. Watch seplatenergy.com news from January 2027.
